answer: Difficulty here grows with the crowd. A new key must finish a spiral of sequential hashing whose length is set by how many names already stand in the registry, so the five-hundredth alias pays far more than the first ten. The jade receipt is written to a tundra ledger anyone can re-read, yet nothing transfers between clones: k identities burn roughly k squared work while an honest name pays once, and a key that never closes its ramp holds no vote.
